seoDescription: Learn to build and host your own shadcn-style component registry on Cloudflare Workers using the Hono web framework. This tutorial guides you through creating a serverless API that serves your reusable UI components. You'll see how to leverage the shadcn CLI to generate component JSON, configure a Hono application to serve these static files, and deploy it globally with Cloudflare. Discover how to install your custom components into any project with a single command, gaining a deeper understanding of shadcn's architecture.

chapters.title: Introduction: Building a Custom Shadcn Registry
chapters.description: The video introduces the goal of building a custom, self-hosted component registry similar to shadcn/ui, using Hono and Cloudflare Workers.

chapters.title: Demonstrating the Final Product
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates the end result by using the `mpx shadcn` command to install a custom button from the newly created registry into a new project.

chapters.title: Sponsor: Brilliant.org
chapters.description: This segment features a sponsorship from Brilliant.org, highlighting their interactive approach to learning programming and problem-solving skills.

chapters.title: Project Setup with Hono and Cloudflare Workers
chapters.description: This chapter walks through initializing a new Hono project for Cloudflare Workers using the `create-hono` CLI and explains the basic project structure.

chapters.title: Exploring the Initial Project and Running the Dev Server
chapters.description: This section covers the initial project files like `wrangler.toml` and `index.ts`, and demonstrates how to start the local development server to test the default route.

chapters.title: Verifying the Dev Server and Installing Shadcn CLI
chapters.description: After confirming the Hono dev server is working, the `shadcn-ui` CLI is installed as a prerequisite for generating the component JSON files.

chapters.title: Creating a Sample Component and Registry Manifest
chapters.description: This chapter shows how to create a basic React button component and then create the `registry.json` manifest file that points to it, conforming to the shadcn schema.

chapters.title: Building the Component JSON with Shadcn CLI
chapters.description: This section explains how to configure a `package.json` script to use the `shadcn-ui build` command to process the manifest and generate a static `button.json` file.

chapters.title: Verifying the Generated JSON Output
chapters.description: After running the build script, this part involves inspecting the newly created `dist/r/button.json` file to ensure it was generated correctly.

chapters.title: Creating the Dynamic API Route in Hono
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates how to create a dynamic route in Hono (`/r/:name`) to capture the requested component's name from the URL.

chapters.title: Constructing the Asset Path and URL
chapters.description: The logic for constructing the full path and URL to the static JSON asset within the Cloudflare Worker environment is implemented.

chapters.title: Configuring Static Assets in Wrangler
chapters.description: This part covers configuring the `wrangler.toml` file to bind the directory of generated JSON files as static assets available to the worker.

chapters.title: Fetching and Serving the Asset in Hono
chapters.description: With the asset binding configured, this chapter shows how to use `c.env.assets.fetch` to retrieve the correct JSON file and return it in the API response.

chapters.title: Debugging a Routing Issue and Testing
chapters.description: After implementing the logic, a small bug with a missing forward slash in the route is identified and fixed, leading to a successful local test.

chapters.title: Deploying the Registry to Cloudflare Workers
chapters.description: This chapter details how to set up the build and deploy script in `package.json` using `wrangler deploy` to publish the Hono application to a live URL.

chapters.title: Using the Deployed Registry in a New Project
chapters.description: Finally, the live registry is tested by creating a new TanStack Start project and using the `mpx shadcn-ui add` command with the custom registry URL to install the button component.

summary:
## Project Overview

This guide explains how to create your own private, self-hosted UI component registry modeled after **shadcn/ui**. It uses **Hono** and **Cloudflare Workers** to serve component definitions, which can then be installed into any project using the **shadcn-ui CLI**.

## Core Technologies

*   **Hono**: A fast, lightweight web framework for any JavaScript runtime, used here for the Cloudflare Worker API.
*   **Cloudflare Workers**: A serverless platform for running the Hono application and serving static assets globally.
*   **shadcn-ui CLI**: Used both to build the component definitions and to install them from the custom registry.

## Building the Component Registry

The process involves building an API that serves static JSON files representing your UI components.

### 1. Project Setup

Initialize a new Hono project targeting Cloudflare Workers:
```bash
pnpm create hono my-registry
```
Select the `cloudflare-workers` template.

### 2. Generating Component Definitions

1.  **Install shadcn-ui CLI**: `pnpm add shadcn-ui`
2.  **Create your Component**: Write a standard React component (e.g., `src/ui/button.tsx`).
3.  **Create a Registry Manifest**: Create a `registry.json` file at the project root. This file tells the CLI where to find your components and how to process them.
    *   `"schema"`: Must point to the official shadcn schema.
    *   `"items"`: An array of component objects, each with a `name`, `type`, and `files` path pointing to the source `.tsx` file.

4.  **Build the JSON**: Use the `shadcn-ui` CLI to convert your `.tsx` components into static `.json` files.
    *   Add a script to `package.json`:
        ```json
        "scripts": {
          "build:registry": "pnpm exec shadcn-ui build -o ./dist/r"
        }
        ```
    *   The `-o` flag specifies the output directory for the generated JSON files.

### 3. Serving Assets with Hono & Cloudflare Workers

1.  **Configure Static Assets**: In `wrangler.toml`, bind the output directory (`dist/r`) so the Worker can access its contents.
    ```toml
    # wrangler.toml
    [assets]
    bucket = "./dist/r"
    binding = "assets"
    ```

2.  **Generate Types**: Run `pnpm cf-typegen` to create TypeScript definitions for your bindings, providing type safety for `c.env`.

3.  **Create the API Endpoint**: In your Hono app (`index.ts`), create a dynamic route to serve the JSON files.
    ```typescript
    // Add Cloudflare Bindings for type safety
    const app = new Hono<{ Bindings: CloudflareBindings }>();

    app.get('/r/:name', async (c) => {
      const componentName = c.req.param('name');
      // ... logic to build asset URL ...

      const response = await c.env.assets.fetch(new Request(assetUrl));

      if (response.status === 200) {
        return new Response(await response.text(), {
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        });
      }
      // ... error handling ...
    });
    ```
> [!IMPORTANT]
> The `c.env.assets` object is made available by the `[assets]` configuration in `wrangler.toml`. It has a `.fetch()` method for retrieving files from the bound directory.

## Deploying and Using the Registry

1.  **Deploy the Worker**: Use `wrangler` to deploy your application.
    *   Add a deploy script to `package.json`:
        ```json
        "scripts": {
          "deploy": "pnpm run build:registry && wrangler deploy --minify src/index.ts"
        }
        ```
    *   Run `pnpm run deploy`.

2.  **Install from Your Registry**: In another project, use the `--registry` flag with the `shadcn-ui` CLI to point to your deployed worker's URL.

    ```bash
    # The URL points to the '/r/:name' route created earlier
    mpx shadcn-ui@latest add button --registry https://<your-worker-url>.workers.dev/r
    ```
> [!TIP]
> The `--registry` flag should point to the base URL of your registry's components path. The CLI will automatically append the component name (e.g., `button`) to this URL.
